## Cleaning data

This is a continuation from importing data.\
\
***Variable naming convention used are :***\
data : main dataframe\
parameter : IMPC parameter data frame\
procedure : IMPC procedure data frame\
disease : Disease information data frame

***Steps***

Data cleaning for main :\
1. correct any eronous data format on each data column\
2. correct appropriate duplicates

Data cleaning for parameter\

## Data Cleaning -Main Data

### 1. Correct erronous data format

*refer to SOP for expected values or data format*

analysis_id

- Found 2 missing analysis_id values and no format mismatches.
- Duplicate values were retained for later cleaning (step 2)

```{r}
#checking NAs and duplicates
sum(is.na(data$analysis_id))
sum(duplicated(data$analysis_id[!is.na(data$analysis_id)]))
#duplicates will be handled on step 2, after all typos and data format is cleaned

#checking if values follow notation of "an" + numbers: 
all(grepl("^an[0-9]{10}$", data$analysis_id[!is.na(data$analysis_id)]))
#TRUE, all values followed the convention, no cleaning needed
```

gene_accession_id

- No missing values or formatting errors were found.

- All 2,846 unique IDs follow the expected MGI format, so no corrections are needed. - The 1,924 IDs absent from the disease reference are retained because that reference is not a complete gene database.

```{r}
#checking missing gene IDs
sum(is.na(data$gene_accession_id))

#checking unexpected ID format
sum(!grepl("^MGI:[0-9]+$", data$gene_accession_id))

#checking unique gene IDs
length(unique(data$gene_accession_id))

#checking IDs against disease reference
length(setdiff(unique(data$gene_accession_id), disease$mgi_id))

#no corrections needed
```

gene_symbol

- Based on the Guidleines for Nomenclature of Genes in Mouse,(<https://www.informatics.jax.org/nomen/gene.shtml?utm_source=chatgpt.com#gnas>), a gene symbol begins with uppercase followed by all lowercase/numbers, with several exceptions :

  - it can start with sequence identifier ex : 0610009F21Rik,

  - it can with start lowercase letter if the gene is only identified by recessive mutant phenotype

  - possible uppercase after the initial letter in certain cases.

- Specific punctuations that are allowed are : hyphens and (). Hyphens are used to separate related sequence and pseudogene symbol from root

```{r}
#remove special characters
data$gene_symbol<- str_remove_all(data$gene_symbol, "[!@#$%^&*+_.]")

#check any remaining mismatch with the conventional gene symbol
unique(data$gene_symbol[
  !grepl("^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$", data$gene_symbol) &
  !is.na(data$gene_symbol)
])

#genes like 1700029H14Rik are acceptable according to guideline
# many lowercase genes seems to be recessive and are acceptable 
# no appropiate use of () found, so we remove
data$gene_symbol<- str_remove_all(data$gene_symbol, "[()]")


# hyphen as initial letter of gene symbol is not part of the guideline's exception so we exclude them
data <- data %>%
  filter(!str_starts(gene_symbol, "-"))


#check remaining possible misspelling
unique(data$gene_symbol[
  !grepl("^[A-Za-z0-9]*$", data$gene_symbol) &
    !is.na(data$gene_symbol)
])


```

strain_name

- No error found

```{r}
#checking unexpected values 
allowed <- c("B6Brd;B6Dnk;B6N-Tyr<c-Brd>", "C57BL/6Brd-Tyr<c-Brd>", "C57BL/6Dnk", "C57BL/6JTyr;C57BL/6N", "C57BL/6N", "C57BL/6NCrl", "C57BL/6NJ", "C57BL/6NTac", "C57BL/6NTacDen")

unique(data$strain_name[!data$strain_name %in% allowed])
unique(data$strain_name[data$strain_name %in% allowed])
table(data$strain_name, useNA = "ifany")
#no unexpected values

```

mouse_life_stage

- 445 errors corrected in life stages

```{r}
correct_names <- c("E9.5", "E12.5", "E15.5", "E18.5", "Early adult", "Middle aged adult", "Late adult")
unique_values <- unique(data$mouse_life_stage)

suggested_corrections <- data.frame(
  original = unique_values,
  suggested = correct_names[
    amatch(unique_values, correct_names, maxDist = 3)
  ]
)
print(suggested_corrections)

data$mouse_life_stage <- correct_names[
  amatch(data$mouse_life_stage,
         correct_names,
         maxDist = 3)
]

#checking if all values are within expected ones
unique(data$mouse_life_stage[!data$mouse_life_stage %in% correct_names])
unique(data$mouse_life_stage[data$mouse_life_stage %in% correct_names])
table(data$mouse_life_stage, useNA = "ifany")
```

parameter_id

- Standardized phenotyping parameters for IMPC IMPReSS database is IMPC_ECG_007_001 (<https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/impc-solr-api/overview-of-key-impc-concepts-and-tools/the-structure-of-impc-data-pipeline-procedure-parameter/>)
- Corrected injections of junk characters

```{r}
#checking missing IDs
sum(is.na(data$parameter_stable_id))

#removing unrelevant characters
data$parameter_stable_id <- str_remove_all(data$parameter_stable_id, "[-!@#$%^&*()+.]")

#checking remaining unexpected characters after removal
sum(!is.na(data$parameter_stable_id) &
      grepl("[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", data$parameter_stable_id)) #0

#make all upper case
data$parameter_stable_id <- toupper(data$parameter_stable_id)

#checking any remaining format error
unique(data$parameter_stable_id[
  !grepl("^[A-Z0-9]+_[A-Z0-9]+_[0-9]+_[0-9]+$", data$parameter_stable_id) &
    !is.na(data$parameter_stable_id)
])

#we have identified several problems : multiple_, and _ in wrong positions

#remove all _ 
x <- str_remove_all(data$parameter_stable_id, "_")

#put _ back in appropriate places
x <- str_replace(x, "^([A-Z]+)([A-Z]{3})(\\d{3})(\\d{3})$", "\\1_\\2_\\3_\\4")   # e.g. IMPC_CSD_039_001
x <- str_replace(x, "^([A-Z]+)(\\d{3})(\\d{3})(\\d{3})$",   "\\1_\\2_\\3_\\4")   # e.g. MGP_026_001_006
data$parameter_stable_id <- x

#checking any remaining format error again
unique(data$parameter_stable_id[
  !grepl("^[A-Z0-9]+_[A-Z0-9]+_[0-9]+_[0-9]+$", data$parameter_stable_id) &
    !is.na(data$parameter_stable_id)
]) #0
```

parameter_name

- No cleaning needed to done

```{r}
View(data)
```

p_value

- 1 row has value 1.1. Changed to NA
- Many pvalue is 0. Assumed its a very small p_value, need to floor it before log transformation later

```{r}
#convert to number
data$p_value <- as.numeric(data$p_value)

#checking unexpected value 
pvalue_check <- data %>% 
  filter(p_value <=0 | p_value >1 | is.na(p_value))
unique(pvalue_check$p_value) #spotted eronous p value of 1.1
#convert pvalue of 1.1 to NA 
data$p_value[data$p_value == 1.1] <-  NA

#there are many p value with 0, possibly due to rounding errors
#we need to floor them later when doing analysis
```

allele_symbol

```{r}
# Symbols safe to exclude from official International COmmittee on Standardized Genetic Nomenclature for Mice are !, @, $, %, ^, &

data$allele_symbol <- str_remove_all(data$allele_symbol, "[!@$%^&]")


```

lacz\_

- 663 typos corrected in lacz_blood, 504 in brain, 575 in colon, 588 in eye, 908 in heart. 604 in kidney, 640 in liver, 600 in lung, 941 in skeletal muscle, 595 in skin, 953 in vascular system.

```{r}
correct_vals <- c("expression", "NA", "no expression", "tissue not available")
# Didn't set the loop here, just change the lacz_* below to the one you want to check
unique_vals <- unique(data$lacz_vascular_system)
suggested_corrections <- data.frame(
  original = unique_vals,
  suggested = correct_vals[
    amatch(unique_vals, correct_vals, maxDist = 3)
  ]
)
print(suggested_corrections)
lacz <- c("lacz_blood", "lacz_brain", "lacz_colon", "lacz_eye", "lacz_heart", "lacz_kidney", "lacz_liver", 
          "lacz_lung", "lacz_skeletal_muscle", "lacz_skin", "lacz_vascular_system")

for (col in lacz){
  data[[col]] <- correct_vals[
    amatch(data[[col]],
           correct_vals,
           maxDist = 3)
  ]
}

#checking if all lacz cols are within expected values 
for (i in lacz) {
  print(unique(data[[i]][!data[[i]] %in% correct_vals]))
  print(unique(data[[i]][data[[i]] %in% correct_vals]))
  print(table(data[[i]], useNA = "ifany"))
}
```

### 2. Correct appropriate duplicates

I tried to analyse if analysis_id is unique and find that there is duplicated files that ends with \_1.csv. I will adjust and do additional cross checking after we have corrected all typos

***dont run this code yet***

```{r}
#! eval : false

#check for duplicates
sum(duplicated(data %>%  select(-file)))
sum(duplicated(data$analysis_id))

dup_id <- data[data$analysis_id %in% data$analysis_id[duplicated(data$analysis_id)],]
View(dup_id)


#id duplicates seems to come from files that ends with _1.csv
#check the number of _1.csv files
sum(grepl("_1.csv$", data$file)) #69 
sum(is.na(data$analysis_id)) #2
#this confirms that id duplicates comes from duplicated file and 2 NAs

#remove duplicates except the NAs
data <- data %>%
  filter(is.na(analysis_id) | !duplicated(analysis_id))
dim(data) 
#27655 - 27586 = 71
#removes 69 "_1.csv" duplicates
# + retain 2 rows with NAs for further analysis
```

## Data Cleaning - Parameter 

- parameters grouped from IMPC website for the testing they are related to.

  - ref_paramater_groups.csv needed is in repo, contains all groups for reference. Some parameters are in twice but with different impcParameterOrigId so these have been retained for now.

- duplicates from impcParameterOrigid removed.

```{r}
# code to group the parameters based on the IMPC protocols
references <- read.csv("./original/ref_paramater_groups.csv", header = TRUE)
View(references)

precleaned_parameter$suffixes <- substr(precleaned_parameter$parameterId, 6, 8)
View(precleaned_parameter)

precleaned_parameter <- precleaned_parameter %>%
 left_join(references, by = "suffixes")

# handling repeats
precleaned_parameter %>%
  filter(duplicated(impcParameterOrigId))
# repeat of GRS parameters found
precleaned_parameter %>%
  filter(duplicated(impcParameterOrigId))
# removing repeats
precleaned_parameter <- precleaned_parameter %>%
  distinct(impcParameterOrigId, .keep_all = TRUE)

parameter <- precleaned_parameter

#checking if there is any duplicated IMPC orig id left 
sum(duplicated(parameter$impcParameterOrigId))

#Verifying all ids are compliant
precleaned_parameter %>%
  filter(!grepl("^IMPC_.{3}_.{3}_.{3}$", parameterId))

```

## Data Cleaning - Disease

- No cleaning needed to be done

```{r}
#Strings variables such as human_name, and do_term are briefly screened for any possible error 
View(disease)
unique(disease$human_name)
unique(disease$do_term)
#No error detected


#checking if human_symbol is uppercased and have no special character
all(grepl("^[A-Z0-9]+$", disease$human_symbol), na.rm = TRUE) #FALSE
#there are some that has, checking 
unique(disease$human_symbol[grepl("[a-z]", disease$human_symbol)])
unique(disease$human_symbol[grepl("[^A-Za-z0-9]", disease$human_symbol)])
# all special characters and lowercase follows convention, no cleaning needed

#checking if mouse_symbol first letter is uppercased and have no special characters
all(grepl("^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$", disease$mouse_symbol), na.rm = TRUE) #FALSE
#there are some that had, checking
unique(disease$mouse_symbol[!grepl("^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$", disease$mouse_symbol)])
#all special characters and lowercase follows convention, no cleaning needed

#Checking if id columns follow their conventions
all(grepl("^HGNC:.*[0-9]+$", disease$hgnc_id), na.rm = TRUE) #TRUE
all(grepl("^DOID:.*[0-9]+$", disease$do_id), na.rm = TRUE) #TRUE
all(grepl("^MGI:.*[0-9]+$", disease$mgi_id), na.rm = TRUE) #TRUE


```

## Data Cleaning - Bespoke

- change the column date into a Date format

```{r}
#Checking if there are special characters in DB obj id 
all(grepl("[a-zA-Z0-9]", bespoke$DB_obj_id), na.rm = TRUE) #TRUE

#Checking if there are special characters, and all gene start with uppercase
all(grepl("^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$", bespoke$DB_obj_symbol), na.rm = TRUE) #FALSE
#there are some that had, checking
unique(bespoke$DB_obj_symbol[!grepl("^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$", bespoke$DB_obj_symbol)])
#all special characters follow convention, no cleaning needed

#checking the notation
all(grepl("^GO:[0-9]", bespoke$GO_id), na.rm = TRUE) #TRUE
all(grepl("^GO_REF:[0-9]", bespoke$DB_reference), na.rm = TRUE) #TRUE

#checking if there are special characters and all starts with uppercase
all(grepl("^[A-Z][a-zA-z0-9]", bespoke$DB_obj_synonym), na.rm = TRUE)
#there are some that has, checking 
unique(bespoke$DB_obj_synonym[!grepl("^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$", bespoke$DB_obj_synonym)])
# all special characters follow convention, no cleaning needed

unique(bespoke$date) #all 20261009
#change into date
bespoke$date <- as.Date(
  format(bespoke$date, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE),
  format = "%Y%m%d"
)

unique(bespoke$DB) #all 1 value
unique(bespoke$Relation) #no other value expcept located_in, enables, involved_in, and part_of
unique(bespoke$DB_obj_type) #all protein
unique(bespoke$taxon) #all taxon: 10090
unique(bespoke$evidence_code) #all value is IEA
unique(bespoke$with_from) #no misspelling
unique(bespoke$aspect) #no other calues than C,F and P
unique(bespoke$DB_obj_name) #brief scanning shows no error
unique(bespoke$assigned_by) #no other value than UniProt and GOC
unique(bespoke$annotation_exp) #all NAs
unique(bespoke$Gene_product_formid) #all NAs
```
